children: U.K. economic growth jumped again in July following a strong start to the year, with activity continuing to perform strongly despite a rise in energy prices due to the war in the Middle East.

Gross domestic product rose 0.4% at the start of the third quarter, following a rise of 0.3% in June, the U.K.'s statistics agency said Friday. This beat a consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal, who expected flat growth.

The data signals continued strength in the U.K. economy following a solid performance in the first half of 2026. GDP has continued to outrun expectations despite persistently elevated energy costs following the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with growth over the second quarter outpacing the U.S. on an annualized basis at 1.7%.

Activity in July was driven by the services sector, while production and construction also picked up, the Office for National Statistics said. Computer programming made the largest contribution, potentially signaling a greater impact from artificial-intelligence activity on the U.K. economy.
"Many of the businesses reporting the largest turnover in July 2026 are involved in activities related to artificial intelligence and cloud computing," the agency said.
It added that hotter weather benefited some businesses while creating challenges for others.

The result will make positive reading for new Prime Minister Andy Burnham as his government seeks to revive an economy that has struggled with low productivity and weak growth for much of the past decade.

In his first speech as U.K. treasury chief on Monday, John Healey said the economy was "turning a corner" as he outlined plans to boost growth via a program of fiscal devolution and an increased focus on business investment. Healey refused to rule out tax rises ahead of the autumn budget.
